Runs boto3 round-trip smoke tests that surface contract subtleties (XML namespace parsing for multipart/tagging/versioning), driving patches. This is contract discovery via verification, but reactive rather than an upfront systematic probe of the signing/error/testid surface.

reasoning: The agent extracted concrete contract points from the spec (error semantics, versioning/delete-marker, XML formats, quota rules) and coded SigV4 header signing from correct recall, matching the level-5 anchor. It reached slightly beyond pure recall by using boto3 round-trips to reveal real contract subtleties (XML namespaces), but never actively probed botocore's canonical-request/presigned/clock-skew internals, never captured signing fixtures, and never enumerated the full testid or error-code surface (the console contract is essentially untouched), so it falls well short of the level-8 'actively probes the real contract' bar. Level 5 is the best fit.
